ev1635260846251.title: Apuan Alps Chestnut Flour
ev1635260846251.description:
Walking between the century-old trunks, people can come across the remains of an old “metato”, a small building used to dry chestnuts. Today, six “metati” are still active and the number has been increasing in recent years. Local people make delicious recipes based on the chestnuts flour: the “castagnaccio” (a chestnut cake scented with orange and rosemary), the “ciacci” (or “necci”) (a chestnut piadina filled with ricotta), and the “ballotti” (sweet chestnuts boiled with fennel seeds).
Video: Garfagnana Dream

ev1636489713034.title: Valorisation and Preservation
ev1636489713034.description: The main outcomes of the chestnut flour value chain are the valorisation and preservation of a local economy but also the maintenance of the local forest management. This value chain contributes to reduce negative trends, e.g. the state of abandon and the loss of historical and cultural heritage.

ev1635247009242.title: Apuan Alps in the Roman Age
ev1635247009242.description:
Raw material extraction was active in the Roman age, and had the greatest development under Julius Caesar.
Export took place through the port of Luni, which is why archaeologists call the Apuan Alps marble “Lunense marble”. The export volume was sufficient to supply the construction of the major public buildings in Rome and the empire, as well as numerous patrician residences. Some of the most important monuments built with the Lunense marble were the Pantheon and Temple of Apollo Palatinus.

ev1635990929081.title: Chestnut Trees
ev1635990929081.description:
In the recent years, natural extraordinary events have increased in frequency up to become ordinary. Fortunately, the damages have always been lower than in 1996.
The Apuan Alps are always beautiful, but especially in May when meadows are covered in a white scented blanket due to thousands of daffodils waving in the wind.
During summer, many tourists visit the Apuan valley for the fresh mountain air close to the seaside. In autumn, the Apuans Alps are covered in golden leaves that fall from the impressive chestnut trees.

ev1635248976084.title: Creation of Apuan Alps Regional Park
ev1635248976084.description: In 1985, the Apuan Alps Regional Park was created to protect the area.

ev1635252161443.title: Regional Park Obtains UNESCO Status
ev1635252161443.description: In 2015, the Apuan Alps Regional Park obtained the status of "UNESCO Global Geopark".

ev1635244689699.title: Natural Description of Apuan Alps
ev1635244689699.description:
The Apuan Alps are a highly suggestive orographic complex, with deep valleys abounding with water. There are very few places in Italy and Europe like the Apuan Alps, which can boast such a natural heritage and richness of landscapes, environment, and naturalistic elements.
Apart from the richness of endemic flora and fauna species, also rocks, minerals, fossils, tectonic structures, superficial and hypogeum morphologies provide unusual, varied, and widespread elements of high environmental value.

ev1635250262309.title: 1996 - Natural Catastrophe
ev1635250262309.description: In High Versilia, in 1996, there was a natural catastrophe which caused about 300 debris flows and overflows of watercourse within few square kilometres. An extraordinary rainfall - amounting to more than 500 mm throughout the day, with peaks of 176 mm/per hour - destroyed many buildings and killed residents, especially in the village of “Cardoso di Stazzema”.

ev1636463298100.title: Chestnut Flour Value Chain
ev1636463298100.description:
The chestnut flour value chain performs various functions: productive, protective, naturalistic, landscape, recreational, and didactic.
This value chain is an example of how traditional productions can contribute to increase the revenue of local population, reducing abandonment, and promoting a balanced relationship between nature and human communities.
Photo: Comune di Fabbriche di Vergemoli

ev1636464702912.title: Local Traditional Food
ev1636464702912.description: Local traditional food is often perceived by consumers having high quality and it is a useful perception to increase touristic appeal, especially if it is supported by recognized high quality standards. For these reasons, chestnut flour value chain can improve the development of resilience initiatives to contemporary challenges.
